summary: The legal one-second timer window permits at most nine invocations; correctness depends on increasing-delay scheduling, numeric identity, independent cancellation, and finite timer cleanup rather than scalable wall-clock growth.

replacement_checks.evidence: The kth cumulative invocation time is k * delay + period * k * (k - 1) / 2; minimum legal delay and period yield nine invocations before 1000 ms, while the tenth is at 1100 ms.
A deterministic fake scheduler verifies successive waits, multiple independent intervals, numeric IDs despite object-valued native handles, cancellation, and the maximum nine-invocation schedule.
Authored cases independently calculate cumulative invocation times and cover cancellation before the first call, exactly at a scheduled time, and both parameter boundaries.
The exact native timer source is remotely Accepted under the provider timeout, and each active task owns only one finite timeout at a time.
